name: clinical_v0_gate36_near_zero
rationale: Composed final-layer weights identify units 198 and 38 as positive readout paths that activate for high normalized values. In 128 calibration patients, their active cases remain underestimated after the original affine correction; almost all are measured variables rather than static/administrative channels. Increase only these two effective output coefficients by 1%, a fixed conservative expansion of the existing learned paths. Negative GELU-tail contributions change in the opposite direction, also consistent with the common positive offset in the low/middle range. No fitting, gradients, optimizer or test data. Exact median-draw activations of the edited model show unit 198 still underestimating in its positive intermediate range (median normalized errors -0.0128, -0.0327, -0.0492 in activation bins 0-0.5, 0.5-1, 1-2), across 93, 81, 96 calibration patients. Above 2 the median error reverses sign to +0.0223. Add a localized triangular correction in preactivation z198: k*(GELU(16*z)-4*GELU(16*(z-1.5))+3*GELU(16*(z-2)))/16, k=0.04*the current effective coefficient. It rises toward the strongest intermediate underestimation and switches off before the high tail. A single fixed 4% slope is used; no fitting or sweep. Reuse three existing neurons with negligible effective contributions. Unit 38 is unchanged because its remaining residual signs are inconsistent. The running benchmark candidate remains unchanged; no clinical test result informed this proposal. Compose the independent 1% sharpening of negative-only head unit 47, using its already specified weights unchanged. The local positive repair reduced mean confirmation MSE but cost MAE; unit 47 sharpening reduced MAE on both confirmation seeds but slightly cost MSE. They address intermediate underestimation and a common positive negative-tail contribution through disjoint neurons. No coefficient is refitted, searched or derived from test. Test their composition as a single new hypothesis, retaining it only if full forward evaluations support joint improvement. New calibration median-draw preactivations show unit 255 remains entirely negative. Its negative coefficient turns GELU's negative lobe into a positive output hump. For z in [-1.5,-1), residual median is +0.00673; for z in [-1,-0.5), it is -0.00197, each across 127 patients. Translate this hump by changing only incoming bias 255 by -0.01. This lowers its left-tail contribution and raises its contribution near zero, unlike uniform attenuation. The pattern is stronger on static/admin/time variables; physiological subgroup signs are mixed. This is one fixed hypothesis on an experimental parent, not a demonstrated causal correction. No gradients, training, parameter sweep or test residuals are used. V1 test scores have already been seen in the ongoing benchmark; any later test is a repeated benchmark assessment. The two positive head paths 38 and 198 have partly aligned incoming weights (cosine 0.69). Normally z38 is below z198. A positive contrast z38-z198 occurs in only 15 median-selected scoring entries across 11 of 512 calibration patients in the gate255 model; its median and mean normalized residuals are negative. Six cases overpredict, so the association is neither universal nor causal proof. An enriched target-free probe shows this contrast remains sparse at both noise steps. Reuse nearly disconnected units 181 and 150 to implement a small capped ramp: A*(GELU(64*d)-GELU(64*(d-1)))/64, d=z38-z198, A=0.05*effective_coefficient38. The zero threshold detects order reversal, the unit contrast caps the response, and the fixed 5% amplitude is not fitted to residual magnitudes. Sharpness confines the small negative GELU lobe near the threshold. No derivatives, training, optimizer, coefficient sweep or test targets are used. This is a new hypothesis requiring complete forward evaluations. Learned path36 has a positive effective readout coefficient, so its negative-GELU shoulder subtracts signal. The preexisting calibration bin[-0.5,0) shows negative final residual means and medians at both noise steps, including the first-only and final-only groups. Physical residual means are negative in all these groups. The same pattern remains after V9. This independent candidate starts from V4 and uses quiet units132,203,34 for A*(GELU(64*(z+0.5))-2*GELU(64*(z+0.25))+GELU(64*z))/64, A=0.05*effective_coefficient36. Support, midpoint, sharpness64 and5% learned-weight fraction are fixed before accuracy evaluation. It contains no V9 or V12 edits; only five final-support entries overlap V9's ideal gate50 support, which is not proof of independent full-model effects. Near-zero calibration residuals and GELU boundary lobes can still lead to overshoot. No gradients, training, residual coefficient fitting, optimizer, parameter sweep, confirmation residuals or test residuals are used.
